newsitem.title: USA: Mistrial for white U.S. cops in black driver death.
newsitem.headline: Mistrial for white U.S. cops in black driver death.

text.p: A judge declared a mistrial on Friday in the racially charged case of two white policemen accused of the suffocation death of a black motorist.

Allegheny County Common Pleas Judge David Cashman made his ruling after Allegheny County Coroner Cyril Wecht gave an interview this week to "Good Morning America" about the case. Defence attorneys also had requested a mistrial after Wecht made certain comments to the all-white jury.

Cashman ruled the interview violated a gag order he had imposed on all court participants. According to local reports, Wecht, who was hired by the victim's family to review the case, said he was unaware the gag order applied to him.

A mistrial does not mean the officers were acquitted and does not preclude a trial at a later date. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court will designate a new county for jury selection and a new jury will be chosen within 120 days.

Brentwood Lt. Milton Mulholland, 57, and Baldwin Patrolman Michael Albert, 32, were charged with one count each of involuntary manslaughter in the Oct. 12, 1995, suffocation death of Jonny Gammage, 31, a cousin and business partner of Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Ray Seals.
Brentwood and Baldwin are Pittsburgh suburbs. Gammage died on a roadside in another suburb, Overbrook, after he was pulled over by Mulholland.

The officers testified in a coroner's inquest that Gammage was driving erratically and became violent when he got out of his car. They said they were forced to restrain him by holding him on the ground.

Black community leaders said they were disappointed with the mistrial ruling. "I was very surprised ... and very disappointed there has to be a break in the trial," said Esther Bush, president of the Urban League of Pittsburgh.
"If this is the way justice has to be served, we'll just have to deal with it. (Gammage) was pulled over for driving erratically, and he's dead. I don't think anybody deserves that."

Patrick Thomassey, defence attorney for the policemen, had requested a mistrial after Wecht said on the witness stand that Mulholland should "explain his role" the night of Gammage's death. He argued that defendants cannot be compelled to testify in such a manner and Wecht's comment could not be stricken from the jurors' minds.
The trial had raised racial tensions here and had been compared with the 1991 beating of black motorist Rodney King by four white police officers whose acquittal sparked major rioting in Los Angeles.

The all-white jury of nine women and three men had been chosen from Chester County in eastern Pennsylvania because of pre-trial publicity. The new jury will not be chosen from either Chester or Allegheny counties.
A third officer who also was charged in the incident, Brentwood Patrolman John Vojtas, will be tried separately. Two other officers who were also at the scene of Gammage's death were not charged.
